app.name: Default Inspector
app.one_liner: See the privacy defaults a multiplayer game sets for your age, why each one exists, and contest any of them.
app.footer: Research prototype by Yuxing Yang. The age-tiered defaults reflect my analysis of the FTC's 2022 case against Epic Games, the UK Age Appropriate Design Code, and the U.S. state design codes I coded. Not legal advice; not affiliated with any game company. Nothing you type leaves this page.
app.try_this: Try this: choose Under 13, then switch to the one-size-fits-all view.

outcome_types.locked: Not changeable at this age. Your objection is still recorded.
outcome_types.parent_approval: This change needs approval from a linked parent account.
outcome_types.with_safeguards: You can change this. It turns on with safeguards, after a plain-language notice.
outcome_types.user_choice: Your choice. The change applies immediately.
outcome_types.revert: Returning to this age's default always applies immediately.
outcome_types.not_applicable: Not applicable: adults have no linked parent account.

settings.label: Text chat with players you don't know

flow.principle: Shared in real time during a match

u13.why: Open chat with strangers is the flow most likely to expose a young child to contact they cannot assess. Parental consent does not change who is on the other end.

safeguards: Only inside your current match or party
Report and block buttons stay visible
teen.notice: Turning this on lets players you don't know read and reply to what you type during matches. They cannot message you privately or hear your voice. You can turn it off any time.
teen.parent_sees: Whether this setting is on. A parent cannot override your choice.
teen.why: Teens are old enough to decide this for themselves, but the default should not decide it for them.

settings.flattened_exposes: Strangers can read and reply to the child's messages during matches.

settings.label: Voice chat with players you don't know

u13.why: A voice reveals more than text: age, mood, sometimes location. This flow stays closed for young children.

teen.why: Teens may open text chat with strangers, but voice stays off: it carries far more personal information than typed text.

settings.flattened_exposes: Strangers can hear the child's voice.

settings.label: Private messages from players you don't know

u13.why: One-to-one contact from strangers, away from the shared space of a match, is where grooming risk concentrates.

teen.why: Contact with strangers is limited to the shared space of a match, where others can see it and report it.

settings.flattened_exposes: Strangers can message the child one-to-one, outside any match.

settings.label: Who can send you friend requests

flow.principle: Accepted requests unlock chat between friends

u13.default: Only people linked through a parent account
options: Only people linked through a parent account
Add one person I know in real life
u13.parent_action: A parent can approve one specific person the child knows offline. Strangers can never be added.
u13.why: Friends should be people a child knows offline. Because friendship unlocks chat, this is the gate that matters most.

teen.why: Teens choose. The default starts at a middle option rather than 'Everyone'.

settings.flattened_exposes: Anyone can send a friend request, and friendship unlocks chat.

settings.label: Your display name shown to other players

flow.principle: Shown on screen during and after matches

u13.parent_action: A parent can allow the name to be shown to approved friends.
u13.why: Children often use real names in display names. Hiding them by default goes beyond what the 2022 order required.

teen.why: Same protective starting point as under 13, but here the teen decides.

settings.flattened_exposes: A real name used as a display name is shown to everyone in the match.

settings.label: What a parent can see about your settings

flow.principle: Visible on request in the parent dashboard

u13.why: Under 13, a verified parent manages these settings.

teen.why: Parents can see what is on, so they can talk about it. They cannot overrule the teen's choice.

settings.flattened_exposes: No parent can see or manage any of these settings.

settings.label: Notifications late at night

flow.principle: Delivered to your phone at any hour

settings.flattened_exposes: The game can wake the child with notifications at any hour.

u13.why: Several state design codes treat lost sleep as a harm of compulsive use, so late-night notifications stay off for minors.

teen.why: The same quiet hours cover ages 13–17. They are set by law, not by the platform.

settings.label: A signal when someone is monitoring your activity

flow.information: The fact that you are being monitored
flow.principle: Shown on screen whenever monitoring is active

settings.flattened_exposes: A parent, or anyone else with access, could monitor the child without the child knowing.

u13.why: Following New Jersey and Vermont, the child is told whenever anyone, a parent included, is monitoring. Maryland's code would let a parent monitor without a signal.

teen.why: Teens always know when they are being watched. The signal protects a teen's autonomy even with respect to a parent.

age_check.u13: Age is self-declared at sign-up; accounts under 13 require a verified parent.

flattened_view.explainer: Many platforms apply one baseline, usually an adult's, to everyone. I call this normative flattening (SOTICS 2026). Turn this on to see the adult defaults applied to the age you selected. Settings that change are highlighted.
flattened_view.summary_template: On a one-size-fits-all platform, {changed} of {total} settings change for this age. {contact} of them open contact with people you don't know.

contest_record.title: Your contest record

who_can_see.teen: You only. A parent sees only the resulting setting.

contest_record.does_not_show: What this record does not show: whether every copy of the old setting (caches, secondary services) has been updated. A trustworthy record should say what it did not check.

basis_labels.analysis: From my analysis of the FTC's 2022 Epic Games case
basis_labels.prototype: Prototype choice: not covered by that analysis, so set by applying the UK Age Appropriate Design Code's high-privacy-by-default standard
basis_labels.law: From the U.S. state design codes I coded in my research-assistant work (preliminary)

general_rules: Any change back to the age band's own default value uses outcome 'revert' (applied immediately), whatever the setting's outcome type.

Each contest record keeps its own status and its own action buttons. While a record for a setting is pending, the Contest button for that setting is replaced by 'Request pending' plus a 'Withdraw' link.
Switching to a different age band marks every pending record as 'Withdrawn: age band changed' and resets values to that band's defaults. Clicking the age band that is already selected does nothing.
Reason text is trimmed before validation; when an objection is required (only one option), whitespace-only text is rejected with an inline message.
